## Final report

**Best design: 2 mm graphite (single layer), evaluation b-0001 (my 5th evaluate call).**

My own judgment against the requirement limits from `brief`:

| Requirement | Limit | Value | Margin | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| THERM-R1-screen | ≤ 420 K | 400.67 K | 19.33 K | pass |
| THERM-R2-hotspot | ≤ 340 K | [335.3104, 335.311] K | ~4.69 K | pass |
| THERM-R3-mass | ≤ 100 kg/m² | 3.6 kg/m² | 96.4 kg/m² | pass |
| THERM-R4-thickness | ≤ 40 mm | 2 mm | 38 mm | pass |

All four requirements pass. Worst margin is on R2 (~4.7 K), which is comfortable given the FE bracket is extremely tight (essentially a point estimate, not a wide uncertainty band).

**Why this is the lightest I believe is achievable here:** the prior constellation's lightest passing design was 10 mm graphite at 18 kg/m². Since the screening/FE hotspot barely moves with thickness in the tested range while mass scales linearly with thickness × density, I tested thinner single-layer designs down to the 1 mm floor (whole-mm constraint). At 1 mm, every material I tried failed R2: graphite (344.4 K), aluminium (340.19 K, fails by 0.19 K), and aluminium nitride (342.5 K, despite AlN's higher conductivity giving it lower mass at 1mm than graphite — its higher density hurts more than its conductivity helps). Graphite has the best conductivity-to-density ratio of the six materials, so at the minimum passing thickness (2 mm) it gives the lowest mass. A multi-layer design can't beat this: any second material at 1mm would only add mass, since no material available is lighter than graphite (except epoxy, whose conductivity is far too low to be viable).

**What I'd try with more budget:** confirm whether a 2mm design mixing a very thin (1mm) high-conductivity cap at the heated face with 1mm graphite could ever beat pure graphite — I judged this dominated (any substitution raises mass) but didn't empirically test a hybrid pair. I'd also want to sanity-check FE bracket stability by re-running 2mm graphite once more (if the tool has any nondeterminism) before treating ~4.7 K as a hard margin.

I used 6/12 evaluations and 11/40 screens, then ran `finish`.
